senses.gloss: (b. h.; cmp. טָרַד)to run about, be busy, to take pains, prepare.
units: <cite ref="Avodah Zarah 3a:10">Ab. Zar. 3ᵃ</cite> <he>מי שט׳ וכ׳</he> he who has made preparations on Friday has food for the Sabbath (he who does good in this world can expect reward in the hereafter).

<cite ref="Ketubot 10a">Keth. 10ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Kiddushin 45b:5">Kidd. 45ᵇ</cite> <he>חזקה אין … טוֹרֵחַ וכ׳</he> the presumption is that one will not go to the trouble of preparing a (wedding) feast and let it go to ruin, i.e. one must have weighty reasons for a divorce immediately after marriage; <cite ref="Yevamot 107a">Yeb. 107ᵃ</cite>.

<cite ref="Berakhot 58a:5">Ber. 58ᵃ</cite>, v. <cite ref="I00223"><he>טוֹרַח</he></cite>; a. fr.—[<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Moed Katan 1:1:3">Y. M. Kat. I, 80ᵃ</cite> bot. <he>דבר שאינו ט׳</he>, v. <cite ref="I00782"><he>טָרֵיחַ</he></cite>.]

senses.gloss: to put to trouble, put a task on.
units: <cite ref="Taanit 24a:4">Taan. 24ᵃ</cite> <he>אתה הִטְרַחְתָּ וכ׳</he> thou hast put thy Creator to the trouble of &c.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 8a:3">Snh. 8ᵃ</cite> <he>מַטְרִיחִין אותי</he> they (the wicked) put me to &c.
<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 27:6">Lev. R. s. 27</cite> <he>לא הִטְרַחְתִּי עליכם</he> I did not tax you too heavily; a. fr.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 22b">Snh. 22ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Eruvin 64b">Erub. 64ᵇ</cite>, a. e., v. <cite ref="I00712"><he>טָרַד</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 244">Yalk. Ex. 244</cite> <he>ה׳ עליו</he> he begged him instantly.
